brief: Since the June 1 Nasdaq top, Fed hike expectations deflated AI-enabler stocks (blue-collar semiconductor names -31%) and independent power producers while bulls rotated into financials; a peak in 2-year yields is keeping mega-cap tech near record highs even as GDP-boom hopes fade. The FOMC statement fell to 130 words, the most terse since 2007. BofA reads returning Fed credibility as long-term bullish for market resilience, but says it requires higher bond risk premiums. Hawkish Fed, BoJ, ECB and BoE view the CPI decline as too slow, while a record net 33% of Fund Manager Survey investors say companies are overinvesting in AI; barring a Trump-Xi trade deal on September 24 or an oil truce (refiners already maxed out), BofA says the best hope for further upside is a peak in hyperscaler capex. Positioning, profits and policy ("3Ps") are all judged to be peaking: the Bull & Bear indicator holds at 9.5 (sell), FMS and hedge-fund positioning are near-record bullish, and 2027 EPS consensus of 10-15% growth requires ISM to stay above 53. BofA says it is not yet time to buy defensives, prefers quality, value and yield, and flags commodities, credit and China bonds as the key Q4 risks.
